text:
Sam: Quick thread for compatibility proxy migration notes. We need a low-risk plan to transition clients off legacy envelope payloads without causing another memory spike.

Priya: Agree. Two parallel tracks: infra mitigation in the proxy, and customer-facing migration for integrators.

Rowan: For infra: add a lightweight admission controller that classifies payloads early and delegates heavy rewrites to a worker pool. Admission keeps request path tiny.

Nate: +1. Worker pool with bounded concurrency will bound allocations and prevent runaway RSS. We can prioritize small requests (embeddings) for fast handling.

Lila: Customer track: notify tenants via console + API header requirement for new envelope format. Offer a "compat opt-out" toggle so tenants can opt to skip rewrites if they’ve migrated.

Sam: Important: telemetry. We need fine-grained counters: legacy_count, migrated_count, rewrite_failures, queue_wait_ms, worker_retries. Also sample payload capture (anonymized).

infra-bot: created ticket INC-3911 for worker-pool approach and telemetry board: https://redwood.internal/inc/3911

Priya: Safety policy: if queue length > 200 or worker backlog > 95th percentile latency threshold, proxy should return 503 with X-Compat-Backpressure: true. Document this behavior in API errors page.

Rowan: Implementation detail: admission controller should be O(1) parse of first ~256 bytes to detect envelope type. No full JSON parse. Use a small state machine.

Nate: We should avoid copying when moving payloads into the worker queue. Use pooled byte buffers and reference counting. Go has sync.Pool; we can wrap with careful lifetime management.

Lila: For customers that can't change immediately, offer a "dedicated migration window" where we run rewriter in sidecar mode with extended timeouts and rate limits to minimize impact on other tenants.

Sam: Timeline suggestion: 1) 3 days: admission + worker pool prototype behind FF, 2) 2 days: telemetry + error semantics, 3) 2 days: console opt-out and API flag, 4) 3 days: staged rollout + load test. Total ~10 working days.

Priya: Add an immediate quick fix: enable gzip passthrough for rewrites (if payloads are compressible) to reduce memory pressure. Small config flip.

Rowan: Risk note: moving to worker pool introduces at-least-once processing semantics if we crash mid-work. Ensure idempotency of rewrites or keep original payload until worker ack.

Nate: Also think about TLS and auth: sidecar workers must not bypass tenant isolation. Use the existing request context with tenant ID and sign tasks for the worker.

Lila: Product asks for a clear deprecation timeline: 90 days after tenant opt-in is available before we remove legacy envelope support for that tenant. We should make this configurable per-tenant.

Sam: Agree. Record deprecation in API docs and send email + in-console banner to high-usage tenants 60 days before enforcement.

Priya: Testing: add unittest for admission DFA, integration test for worker queue overload, and e2e migration test with sample SDKs. Also a chaos test that kills workers mid-rewrite.

Rowan: Add log fields: compat_path=admit|worker|sidecar, tenant_id, trace_id, rewrite_ms, mem_before, mem_after. Keep logs structured for alerting.

Nate: For rollout: start with internal tenants, then beta tenants who opt-in, then general availability. Gate each phase on mem/latency signals.

Lila: UX: the console toggle shows "Skip rewrites (fastpath)" with tooltip: "If enabled, Redwood will not rewrite legacy envelopes for this tenant. Only enable if your integrations use vX envelopes."

Sam: Security check: data residency. If we offload rewrites to a worker pool that runs in different AZs, ensure data never crosses tenant-defined regions. Respect Private deployment constraints.

Priya: Ops: add a kill-switch feature flag with automatic rollback conditions: sustained mem > 75% for 3m or error rate > 2% for 5m. This flips the feature off globally.

infra-bot: snapshot of current metrics posted: grafana.redwood/compat-proxy/overload (link)

Rowan: Code note: small admission state machine pseudocode: ```
state = START
for b in buf[:256]:
  switch state:
    case START: if b == '{' state=OBJ
    case OBJ: if sequence matches "envelope" return LEGACY
return UNKNOWN
```
Keep it tiny.

Nate: Owner assignments? I'll implement worker pool + buffer pool proto. Rowan will build admission DFA and unit tests. Priya owns telemetry + alerts. Lila owns tenant UX + deprecation comms. Sam will coordinate rollout and security checks.

Lila: I'll draft the customer email and console copy and share in this thread.

Sam: Great. Please add estimated PRs and link them here when opened. We'll track in INC-3911. :thumbsup:
